stem: Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
hints: All three fractions have the same bottom number, 7.
When the bottoms are the same, the fraction with the bigger top is the bigger fraction.
Put the tops in order from smallest to largest, then find the list that matches.

steps.action: Notice that 1/7, 3/7 and 6/7 all have the same bottom number, 7.
steps.why: The same bottom means the pieces are the same size: sevenths.

steps.action: Compare the tops: 1 is less than 3, and 3 is less than 6.
steps.why: When the pieces are the same size, more pieces means a bigger amount. 6 sevenths is more than 3 sevenths.

steps.action: From smallest to largest, the order is 1/7, 3/7, 6/7.

trapNotes.6/7, 3/7, 1/7: This list goes from largest to smallest. The question asks for the smallest first.
trapNotes.3/7, 1/7, 6/7: This starts with 3/7, but 1/7 is smaller than 3/7. The smallest must come first.
trapNotes.1/7, 6/7, 3/7: This puts 6/7 before 3/7. But 6/7 is bigger, so it must come last.
